summary.intent: Implement GitHub issue #618 (deterministic-CBOR codec + KAT test-vector spine for cipher-box's core crate) while fanning out other independent v2-build issues (#624 API auth, #623 engine scaffold, #645 Tauri shell) to background worktree agents, then run a crypto/privacy security review on the resulting PR.
summary.outcome: #618 was implemented, self-reviewed (standards + spec agents), fixed, verified green natively and under wasm32-wasip1, committed, and merged as PR #659 with a new required CI check registered on main. #624, #623, and #645 completed in parallel worktrees awaiting user review/merge. A crypto-privacy-review report was generated and committed to .planning/security/REVIEW-2026-07-20-pr659.md.

repo: crates/core/src must have zero I/O/clock/RNG (doctrine enforced in standards review) — example binaries like kat_gen are exempt.

Error surface in crates/core/src/error.rs uses a two-class model (trust vs malformed) with uniquely named checks; the trust/malformed boundary for tags/floats/simple-values is a frozen judgement call requiring explicit human sign-off since re-classing later breaks committed KAT vectors.
proptest's `fork` feature (via wait-timeout) doesn't compile on wasm32-wasip1 — must split the proptest dev-dependency per-target (forkless config for wasm) in Cargo.toml.

CI `rust` path filter must include every file that affects the job's inputs (missed `.cargo/config.toml`, which affects the wasmtime runner, initially) — path filters need auditing whenever new config files are added.
Naming a CI job merge-blocking isn't enough; it must also be separately registered as a required status check in branch protection.
lint-staged prettier reformatting a generator-owned artifact (openapi.json) silently breaks its freshness diff check — needed a .prettierignore exclusion so the generator alone owns those bytes.

Half-float bit patterns can alias simple values in CBOR decoding (e.g. f90014 vs `false`) — dispatch must key on additional-info bits, not naive value comparison; this is now pinned as a KAT regression vector.

A KAT-vector generator that preserves manifest header fields (manifestVersion/profile/structureTags/kdfEdges) from the existing file-on-disk (rather than regenerating them) lets hand-edits survive the freshness diff, undermining the 'committed generator is sole writer' guarantee.
v1's `@Throttle` decorator was inert in production; the new API auth slice explicitly asserts the ThrottlerGuard fires real 429s via supertest against the live Nest app to prevent regression.
Repo convention for auth revocation is hard-delete rows, never soft-flag/revoke fields.

code.finding: Trust/malformed classification boundary (indefinite-length=trust; tags/floats/oversize-simple-values=malformed) is not derivable from blueprint/core.md and needed an explicit rationale comment added post-review.

build_manifest previously preserved manifestVersion/profile/structureTags/kdfEdges from the existing file on disk instead of regenerating them; fixed to hardcode these so the generator is the sole writer of every manifest byte.
`rust` path filter omitted `.cargo/config.toml`, so changes to the wasm runner config could skip the core-kats job; fixed by adding it to the filter.

workflow: Before fanning out new parallel work, check open issues' 'Depends on:' lines against what's already in flight to find genuinely independent slices to background.

After a background worktree agent reports completion, verify its claims on disk (branch exists, commits present, working tree clean) before repeating its report to the user — treat agent self-reports as unverified until checked.

Run two independent review agents (standards-compliance and spec-fidelity) in parallel against a diff before opening a PR, then fix actionable findings and re-verify (tests/clippy/fmt/wasm) before committing.
Flag architecture-defining slices (e.g. #623 engine scaffold, which downstream slices build on) for mandatory human review before merge, even when built by an agent.

friction: proptest's fork/wait-timeout dependency broke the wasm32-wasip1 test build, requiring a per-target Cargo.toml split.
lint-staged prettier was reformatting the generated openapi.json and silently breaking the CI freshness check.
CI path filter for the rust job was incomplete (missing .cargo/config.toml), a latent gap only caught by the standards review agent.
kat_gen.rs generator had a design flaw (preserving stale manifest header fields from disk) that weakened its own freshness guarantee — only caught by review, not by initial implementation or tests.
Registering a CI job as merge-blocking in branch protection is a separate manual step from naming the job in ci.yml, easy to forget (flagged by spec review as unresolved until fixed).
open_items: #623 engine scaffold (architecture-defining) still needs a human review pass before merge.

#624 and #645 branches need a rebase to pick up the newly-registered 'Core KATs (native + WASM)' required check.
